title: Notation
body_md: $\mathbb{N}$, $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{R}^d$ denote positive integers, real numbers and $d$-dimensional vectors. For $m \in \mathbb{N}$, $[m]$ denotes positive integers up to and including $m$. $\langle \cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the Euclidean inner product, while $\|\cdot\|$ is the induced vector/matrix norm. Subscripts denote agents and superscripts denote the iteration, e.g., $x^t_i$ refers to agent $i$'s model in iteration $t$. The ``big O'' notation $\mathcal{O}(\cdot)$ hides global constants, while $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\cdot)$ additionally hides poly-logarithmic factors, unless stated otherwise.
head: manual

label: asmpt:network
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{asmpt:network}
    The weight matrix $W \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ is primitive, doubly stochastic, and it holds that $\|W - \frac{1}{n}\mathbf{1}_n\mathbf{1}_n^\top\| < 1$, where $\mathbf{1}_n \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is the vector of all ones.
head: environment

label: asmpt:initialization
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{asmpt:initialization}
    Agents' initial models $x_i^1 \in \mathbb{R}^d$, $i \in [n]$, are deterministic quantities. Moreover, agents share the initialization, i.e., $x_i^1 = x_j^1$, for all $i, j \in [n]$.
head: environment

label: asmpt:cost
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{asmpt:cost}
    The global cost is bounded from below and agents' costs have $L$-Lipschitz gradients, i.e., $f^\star \coloneqq \inf_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x) > -\infty$ and for all $i \in [n]$ and $x, y\in \mathbb{R}^d$, we have $\|\nabla f_i(x) - \nabla f_i(y)\| \leq L\|x - y\|$.
head: environment

label: asmpt:bdd-het
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{asmpt:bdd-het}
    There exist constants $A,B \geq 0$ (with at least one strictly positive), such that for all $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and $i \in [n]$, we have $\|\nabla f_i(x)\|^2 \leq A^2 + B^2\|\nabla f(x)\|^2$.

label: lm:sadiev
title: Lemma

title: Lemma
body_md:
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be independent random vectors and let $x_i = \mathbb{E}[X_i]$ and $\widetilde{X}_i = \texttt{clip}(X_i)$, $i \in [n]$ be the expectation and clipped version, with $\overline{x} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i \in [n]}x_i$ and $\widetilde{X} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i \in [n]}\widetilde{X}_i$ being the averaged values. If for some $\sigma_i > 0$ and $p \in (1,2]$ we have $\mathbb{E}\|X_i - x_i\|^p \leq \sigma_i^p$ and $\|x_i\| \leq \nicefrac{\gamma}{2}$, then
    \begin{align*}
        &\|\mathbb{E}[\widetilde{X}] - \overline{x}\| \leq \frac{4\sigma^p}{\gamma^{p-1}}, \\
        &\mathbb{E}\|\widetilde{X} - \mathbb{E}[\widetilde{X}]\|^2 \leq \frac{18\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^p}{n}, 
    \end{align*} where $\sigma^p = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i \in [n]}\sigma_i^p$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Using Jensen's inequality and \eqref{eq:bias-bdd}, we then get
    \begin{equation*}
        \|\mathbb{E}[\widetilde{X}] - \overline{x}\| \leq \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\mathbb{E}[\widetilde{X}_i] - \overline{x}\| \leq \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i \in [n]}\frac{4\sigma_i^p}{\gamma^{p-1}} = \frac{4\sigma^p}{\gamma^{p-1}},
    \end{equation*} proving the first claim. Next, using the fact that $X_i$'s are independent, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}\|\widetilde{X} - \mathbb{E}[\widetilde{X}]\|^2 &= \frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{i \in [n]}\mathbb{E}\|\widetilde{X}_i - \mathbb{E}[\widetilde{X}_i]\|^2 + \frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{j \neq i}\mathbb{E}\big\langle \widetilde{X}_i - \mathbb{E}[\widetilde{X}_i], \widetilde{X}_j - \mathbb{E}[\widetilde{X}_j]\big\rangle \\ 
        &= \frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{i \in [n]}\mathbb{E}\|\widetilde{X}_i - \mathbb{E}[\widetilde{X}_i]\|^2 \leq \frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{i \in [n]}18\gamma^{2-p}\sigma_i^p = \frac{18\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^p}{n},
    \end{align*} where the inequality follows from \eqref{eq:variance-bdd}, completing the proof.

title: Proof
body_md:
Starting from the update rule \eqref{eq:gt-model-update}, it then follows that
    \begin{align*}
        \|{\mathbf x^{t+1}} - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^{t+1}\| &= \|(\mathbf{W} - \mathbf{J})({\mathbf x^{t}} - \alpha\widetilde{\mathbf{g}}^t)\| = \|(\mathbf{W} - \mathbf{J})({\mathbf x^{t}} - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^t - \alpha\widetilde{\mathbf{g}}^t)\| \\
        &\leq \lambda\|{\mathbf x^{t}} - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^t - \alpha \widetilde{\mathbf{g}}^t\| \leq \lambda\|{\mathbf x^{t}} - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^t\| + \alpha\lambda\|\widetilde{\mathbf{g}}^t\| \leq \lambda\|{\mathbf x^{t}} - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^t\| + \alpha\gamma\lambda\sqrt{n}, 
    \end{align*} where the last inequality follows from the fact that $\|\widetilde{\mathbf{g}}^t\| \leq \gamma\sqrt{n}$. Iterating the inequality recursively, we get
    \begin{align*}
        \|{\mathbf x^{t+1}} - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^{t+1}\| \leq \lambda^t\|{\mathbf x}^1 - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^1\| + \alpha\gamma\sqrt{n}\sum_{k = 1}^{t-1}\lambda^{t-k} \stackrel{(i)}{=} \alpha\gamma\lambda\sqrt{n}\sum_{k = 1}^{t-1}\lambda^{t-1-k} \leq \frac{\alpha\gamma\lambda\sqrt{n}}{1-\lambda}, 
    \end{align*} with $(i)$ following from the shared initialization. Next, noting that $\|x^t_i - \overline{x}^t\|^2 \leq \sum_{i \in [n]}\|x^t_i - \overline{x}^t\|^2 = \|{\mathbf x^{t}} - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^t\|^2$, it then follows that, for any $i \in [n]$ and $t \geq 1$, we have
    \begin{equation*}
        \|x^{t+1}_i - \overline{x}^{t+1}\| \leq \|{\mathbf x^{t+1}} - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^{t+1}\| \leq \frac{\alpha\gamma\lambda\sqrt{n}}{1-\lambda},
    \end{equation*} completing the proof.
head: environment

label: eq:cons-gap-bdd
title: Proof
body_md:
Starting from the update rule \eqref{eq:gt-model-update} and defining $X^t \coloneqq \frac{\|{\mathbf x^{t}} - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^t\|^2}{n}$, it follows that for any $t \geq 1$, we have
    \begin{align*}
        X^{t+1} \leq \frac{1+\lambda^2}{2}X^t + \frac{2\alpha^2\lambda^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)}\|\widetilde{\mathbf{g}}^t\|^2 \leq \frac{1+\lambda^2}{2}X^t + \frac{4\alpha^2\lambda^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)}\big(\|\widetilde{\mathbf{g}}^t - \nabla \mathbf{f}^t\|^2 + \|\nabla \mathbf{f}^t\|^2\big), 
    \end{align*} where $(i)$ follows from Young's inequality, i.e., $(a+b)^2 \leq (1+\theta)a^2 + (1+\theta^{-1})b^2$ with $\theta = \frac{1-\lambda^2}{2\lambda^2}$, while in $(ii)$ we again used Young's inequality with $\theta = 1$. Iterating the inequality recursively, denoting by $Y^t \coloneqq \|\widetilde{\mathbf{g}}^t - \nabla \mathbf{f}^t\|^2 + \|\nabla \mathbf{f}^t\|^2$ and noting that $X^1 = 0$, we get
    \begin{align}\label{eq:cons-gap-bdd}
        X^{t+1} \leq \frac{4\alpha^2\lambda^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)}\sum_{k = 1}^{t}\bigg(\frac{1+\lambda^2}{2}\bigg)^{t-k}Y^k. 
    \end{align} We next proceed to bound $Y^k$. To that end, we have
    \begin{align*}
        Y^k &= \|\widetilde{\mathbf{g}}^k - \nabla \mathbf{f}^k\|^2 + \|\nabla \mathbf{f}^k\|^2 = \sum_{i \in [n]}\big(\|\widetilde{g}^k_i - \nabla f_i(x^k_i)\|^2 + \|\nabla f_i(x^k_i)\|^2\big) \\
        &= \sum_{i \in [n]}\big(\|\widetilde{g}^k_{i,b} + \widetilde{g}^k_{i,u}\|^2 + \|\nabla f_i(x^k_i)\|^2\big) \leq 2\sum_{i \in [n]}\big(\|\widetilde{g}^k_{i,b}\|^2 + \|\widetilde{g}^k_{i,u}\|^2 + A^2 + B^2\|\nabla f(x^k_i)\|^2\big),
    \end{align*} where the last inequality follows from Assumption \ref{asmpt:bdd-het}. Plugging the above bound into \eqref{eq:cons-gap-bdd} completes the proof.

label: lm:descent-sharp
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Starting from Lemma \ref{lm:descent-inequality}, rearranging and summing up to time $T$, we get
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{\alpha}{4}\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\nabla f(\overline{x}^t)\|^2 &\leq \Delta_1 - \Delta_{T+1} - \alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\langle \nabla f(\overline{x}^t), \widehat{g}^t_u\rangle \\ &+ 2\alpha^2L\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 + 2\alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_b\|^2 + \frac{\alpha L^2}{2n}\sum_{t \in [T]}\|{\mathbf x^{t}} - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^t\|^2. 
    \end{align*} Next, using the fact that $\|\nabla f(\overline{x}^t)\|^2 \geq \frac{1}{2n}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\nabla f(x^t_i)\|^2 - \frac{L^2}{n}\|{\mathbf x^{t}} - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^t\|^2$, it follows that
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{\alpha}{8n}&\sum_{t \in [T]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\nabla f(x^t_i)\|^2 \leq \Delta_1 - \Delta_{T+1} - \alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\langle \nabla f(\overline{x}^t), \widehat{g}^t_u\rangle \\
        &+ 2\alpha^2L\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 + 2\alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_b\|^2 + \frac{3\alpha L^2}{4n}\sum_{t \in [T]}\|{\mathbf x^{t}} - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^t\|^2. 
    \end{align*} Applying Lemma \ref{lm:consensus-bound}, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{\alpha}{8n}\sum_{t \in [T]}\sum_{i \in [n]}&\|\nabla f(x^t_i)\|^2 \leq \Delta_1 - \Delta_{T+1} - \alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\langle \nabla f(\overline{x}^t), \widehat{g}^t_u\rangle + 2\alpha^2L\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 + 2\alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_b\|^2 \\
        &+ \frac{6\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)}\sum_{t \in [T]}\sum_{k = 1}^t\bigg(\frac{1+\lambda^2}{2}\bigg)^{t-k}\sum_{i \in [n]}\big(\|\widetilde{g}^k_{i,b}\|^2 + \|\widetilde{g}^k_{i,u}\|^2 + A^2 + B^2\|\nabla f(x^k_i)\|^2 \big) \\
        &\leq \Delta_1 - \Delta_{T+1} - \alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\langle \nabla f(\overline{x}^t), \widehat{g}^t_u\rangle + 2\alpha^2L\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 + 2\alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_b\|^2 \\
        &+ \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{i \in [n]}\sum_{t \in [T]}\big(\|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,b}\|^2 + \|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,u}\|^2 + A^2 + B^2\|\nabla f(x^t_i)\|^2 \big),
    \end{align*} where in the second inequality we used the fact that for any non-negative sequence $\{a_t\}_{t \in \mathbb{N}}$ and $\lambda \in [0,1)$
    \begin{equation*}
        \sum_{t \in [T]}\sum_{k \in [t]}a_k\lambda^{t-k} = \sum_{t \in [T]}a_t\sum_{k \in [t]}\lambda^{t-k} \leq \frac{1}{1-\lambda}\sum_{t \in [T]}a_t.
    \end{equation*} Rearranging the terms and noting that $\alpha \leq \frac{1-\lambda^2}{8\lambda LB\sqrt{3}}$ implies $\frac{\alpha}{8} - \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{(1-\lambda^2)^2} \geq \frac{\alpha}{16}$, we then get
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{\alpha}{16n}&\sum_{t \in [T]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\nabla f(x^t_i)\|^2 \leq \Delta_1 - \Delta_{T+1} - \alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\langle \nabla f(\overline{x}^t), \widehat{g}^t_u\rangle + 2\alpha^2L\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 \\
        &+ 2\alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_b\|^2 + \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2A^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2} + \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{i \in [n]}\sum_{t \in [T]}\big(\|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,b}\|^2 + \|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,u}\|^2\big),
    \end{align*} which completes the proof.

label: lm:desirable-event
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:good-event-property
title: Proof
body_md:
We prove the result by induction on $N$. For $N = 1$ we have $\Delta_1 \geq 0$, which holds trivially. Next, assume that for some $N \in [T]$, we have $\mathbb{P}(\Gamma_N) \geq 1 - \frac{(N-1)\delta}{T}$. Using Lemma \ref{lm:descent-sharp} and rearranging, it follows that under $\Gamma_N$, we have for any $t \in [N]$
    \begin{align}\label{eq:good-event-property}
        \Delta_{t} &\leq \Delta_1 - \alpha\sum_{k \in [t-1]}\langle \nabla f(\overline{x}^k), \widehat{g}^k_u\rangle + 2\alpha^2L\sum_{k \in [t-1]}\|\widehat{g}^k_u\|^2 + 2\alpha\sum_{k \in [t-1]}\|\widehat{g}^k_b\|^2 \nonumber \\
        &+ \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2A^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2} + \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{k \in [t-1]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\big(\|\widetilde{g}^k_{i,b}\|^2 + \|\widetilde{g}^k_{i,u}\|^2\big) \leq 2\Delta_1.
    \end{align} From the smoothness of $f$ and \eqref{eq:good-event-property}, it follows that for all $t \in [N]$ on $\Gamma_N$ we have
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:global-grad-bdd}
        \|\nabla f(\overline{x}^t)\| \leq \sqrt{2L\Delta_t} \leq 2\sqrt{L\Delta_1}.
    \end{equation} Using the heterogeneity bound, it can then be seen that for any $i \in [n]$ and $t \in [N]$
    \begin{align}\label{eq:local-grad-bdd}
        \|\nabla f_i(x^t_i)\| &\leq L\|x^t_i - \overline{x}^t\| + \|\nabla f_i(\overline{x}^t)\| \leq L\|{\mathbf x^{t}} - \overline{{\mathbf x}}^t\| + A + B\|\nabla f(\overline{x}^t)\| \nonumber \\
        &\stackrel{(i)}{\leq} \frac{\alpha\gamma\lambda L\sqrt{n}}{1-\lambda} + A + 2B\sqrt{L\Delta_1} \stackrel{(ii)}{\leq} \frac{\lambda L\sqrt{n}}{1-\lambda} + A + 2B\sqrt{L\Delta_1} \stackrel{(iii)}{\leq} \frac{\gamma}{2},
    \end{align} where $(i)$ follows from Lemma \ref{lm:consensus-crude}, $(ii)$ follows from the choice of step-size, while $(iii)$ follows from the choice of clipping threshold. We will now show that $\Gamma_{N+1}$ holds with probability at least $1 - \frac{N\delta}{T}$. In particular, we will show that $\Gamma_N \cap A \subseteq \Gamma_{N+1}$ for some event $A$, allowing us to focus on the part of the probability space where $\Gamma_N$ holds. Using the bound in Lemma \ref{lm:descent-sharp} with $T = N$ and the fact that the left-hand side is non-negative, we get
    \begin{align*}
        &\quad\quad\Delta_{N+1} \leq \Delta_1 - \alpha\sum_{t \in [N]}\langle \nabla f(\overline{x}^t), \widehat{g}^t_u\rangle + 2\alpha^2L\sum_{t \in [N]}\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 + 2\alpha\sum_{t \in [N]}\|\widehat{g}^t_b\|^2 \\
        &+ \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2A^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2} + \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{t \in [N]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,b}\|^2 + \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{t \in [N]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,u}\|^2.
    \end{align*} Next, we construct martingale difference sequences by adding and subtracting $\mathbb{E}_t\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2$ and $\mathbb{E}_t\|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,u}\|^2$. For ease of notation, define $\theta^t \coloneqq \|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 - \mathbb{E}_t\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2$ and $\eta^t_i \coloneqq \|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,u}\|^2 - \mathbb{E}_t\|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,u}\|^2$. We then have
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:induction-step-1}
    \begin{aligned}
        &\Delta_{N+1} \leq \Delta_1 - \alpha\sum_{t \in [N]}\langle \nabla f(\overline{x}^t), \widehat{g}^t_u\rangle + 2\alpha^2L\sum_{t \in [N]}\theta^t + 2\alpha^2L\sum_{t \in [N]}\mathbb{E}_t\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 + 2\alpha\sum_{t \in [N]}\|\widehat{g}^t_b\|^2 \\
        &+ \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2A^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2} + \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{t \in [N]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,b}\|^2 + \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{t \in [N]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\big(\eta^t_i + \mathbb{E}_t\|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,u}\|^2\big).
    \end{aligned}
    \end{equation} Recalling that we are focused on the event where $\Gamma_N$ holds and using \eqref{eq:local-grad-bdd}, we can then apply Lemmas \ref{lm:noise-behavior} and \ref{lm:sadiev} to bound some of the terms in \eqref{eq:induction-step-1}, as follows
    \begin{equation*}
        \|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,b}\|^2 \leq \frac{4\sigma^{2p}}{\gamma^{2(p-1)}}, \:\: \|\widehat{g}^t_b\|^2 \leq \frac{4\sigma^{2p}}{\gamma^{2(p-1)}}, \:\: \mathbb{E}_t\|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,u}\|^2 \leq 18\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^p \: \text{ and } \mathbb{E}_t\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 \leq \frac{18\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^p}{n}.  
    \end{equation*} Plugging back into \eqref{eq:induction-step-1} and recalling that $N \leq T$, we get
    \begin{align}\label{eq:induction-step-2}
        &\Delta_{N+1} \leq \Delta_1 - \alpha\sum_{t \in [N]}\langle \nabla f(\overline{x}^t), \widehat{g}^t_u\rangle + 2\alpha^2L\sum_{t \in [N]}\theta^t + \frac{36\alpha^2\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^pLT}{n} + \frac{8\alpha\sigma^{2p}T}{\gamma^{2(p-1)}} \nonumber \\
        &+ \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2A^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2} + \frac{48\alpha^3\sigma^{2p}\lambda^2L^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2\gamma^{2(p-1)}} + \frac{216\alpha^3\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^p\lambda^2L^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2} + \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{t \in [N]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\eta^t_i.
    \end{align} We now focus on bounding the remaining three terms in \eqref{eq:induction-step-2}, i.e., $B_1 = \alpha\sum_{t \in [N]}\langle \nabla f(\overline{x}^t), \widehat{g}^t_u\rangle$, $B_2 = 2\alpha^2L\sum_{t \in [N]}\theta^t$ and $B_3 = \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{t \in [N]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\eta^t_i$.
    
    \paragraph{Bounding $B_1$.} We define the variable $Z^t = \begin{cases} \nabla f(\overline{x}^t), & \text{if } \Delta_t \leq 2\Delta_1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$. From the definition of $Z^t$ it follows that $\|Z^t\| \leq 2\sqrt{L\Delta_1}$, while from the definition of $\widehat{g}^t_u$ it follows that $\|\widehat{g}^t_u\| \leq 2\gamma$, therefore $\langle Z^t,\widehat{g}^t_u\rangle \leq 4\gamma\sqrt{L\Delta_1}$, almost surely. Further, it can be seen that $\mathbb{E}_t\langle Z^t,\widehat{g}^t_u\rangle = 0$, making $\langle Z^t,\widehat{g}^t_u\rangle$ a bounded martingale difference sequence. Applying Lemma \ref{lm:freedman}, we get
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathbb{P}\Big(\Big|\sum_{t \in [N]}\alpha\langle Z^t, \widehat{g}^t_u \rangle\Big| > b \text{ and } \sum_{t \in [N]}\alpha^2\mathbb{E}_t\big[\langle Z^t, \widehat{g}^t_u\rangle^2\big] \leq c \Big) \leq 2\exp\bigg(-\frac{b^2}{2c + 8\alpha\gamma b\sqrt{L\Delta_1}/3} \bigg),
    \end{equation*} for any $b, c > 0$. Choosing $c = C\log\big(\frac{6T}{\delta}\big)$ for some $C > 0$ (to be specified later) and 
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:bound-B1}
        b = \log\bigg(\frac{6T}{\delta}\bigg)\Bigg(\frac{4}{3}\alpha\gamma\sqrt{L\Delta_1} + \sqrt{\frac{16}{9}\alpha^2\gamma^2L\Delta_1 + 2C}\Bigg),    
    \end{equation} results in
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:prob-bound-1}
        2\exp\bigg(-\frac{b^2}{2c + 8\alpha\gamma b\sqrt{L\Delta_1}/3} \bigg) = \frac{\delta}{3T}.
    \end{equation} Next, recalling \eqref{eq:good-event-property}, it follows that $Z^t = \nabla f(\overline{x}^t)$ for all $t \in [N]$ on $\Gamma_N$, therefore $B_1 = \alpha\sum_{t \in [N]}\langle -Z^t,\widehat{g}^t_u\rangle$ on $\Gamma_N$. Further, under $\Gamma_N$, it holds that
    \begin{align}\label{eq:var-ineq-1}
        \sum_{t \in [N]}\alpha^2\mathbb{E}_t\big[\langle -Z^t, \widehat{g}^t_u\rangle^2\big] &\leq \sum_{t \in [N]}\alpha^2\mathbb{E}_t\|Z^t\|^2\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 \leq 4\alpha^2L\Delta_1\sum_{t \in [N]}\mathbb{E}_t\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 \nonumber \\
        &\stackrel{(i)}{\leq} \frac{72\alpha^2\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^pL\Delta_1N}{n} \leq \frac{72\alpha^2\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^pL\Delta_1T}{n},
    \end{align} where $(i)$ follows from Lemma \ref{lm:noise-behavior}. Therefore, choosing $C = \frac{72\alpha^2\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^pL\Delta_1T}{n}$ and defining the event $\Xi_1 = \big\{\omega: B_1(\omega) \leq b \big\}$, where $b$ is given in \eqref{eq:bound-B1}, it follows that
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{P}(\Gamma_N \cap \Xi_1) &= \mathbb{P}\Big( \Gamma_N \cap \Big\{\sum_{t \in [N]}\alpha\langle-Z^t,\widehat{g}^t_u\rangle \leq b\Big\} \Big) \\ 
        &\stackrel{(a)}{=} \mathbb{P}\bigg( \Gamma_N \cap \bigg\{\sum_{t \in [N]}\alpha\langle-Z^t,\widehat{g}^t_u\rangle \leq b \:\text{ or } \sum_{t \in [N]}\alpha^2\langle -Z^t,\widehat{g}^t_u\rangle^2 > C\log\bigg(\frac{6T}{\delta}\bigg) \bigg\} \bigg) \\
        &\stackrel{(b)}{\geq} 1 - \mathbb{P}(\Gamma_N^c) - \mathbb{P}\bigg(\sum_{t \in [N]}\alpha\langle-Z^t,\widehat{g}^t_u\rangle > b \: \text{ and } \sum_{t \in [N]}\alpha^2\langle -Z^t,\widehat{g}^t_u\rangle^2 \leq C\log\bigg(\frac{6T}{\delta}\bigg) \bigg\}\bigg) \\
        &\stackrel{(c)}{\geq} 1 - \frac{(N-1)\delta}{T} - \frac{\delta}{3T} = 1 - \frac{(N-2/3)\delta}{T}.
    \end{align*} where $(a)$ follows from \eqref{eq:var-ineq-1} and the choice of $C$, in $(b)$ we used $\mathbb{P}(A\cap B) \geq 1 - \mathbb{P}(A^c) - \mathbb{P}(B^c)$, while $(c)$ follows from \eqref{eq:prob-bound-1} and the induction hypothesis. 
    
    \paragraph{Bounding $B_2$.} Recall that $B_2 = 2\alpha^2L\sum_{t \in [N]}\theta^t$, where $\theta^t = \|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 - \mathbb{E}_t\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2$. By definition, we know that $\mathbb{E}_t[\theta^t] = 0$ and $|2\alpha^2L\theta^t| \leq 16\alpha^2\gamma^2L$, hence we can apply Lemma \ref{lm:freedman}, to get
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathbb{P}\Big(\big| B_2 \big| > d \text{ and } \sum_{t \in [N]}4\alpha^4L^2\mathbb{E}_t\big[(\theta^t)^2\big] \leq e \Big) \leq 2\exp\bigg(-\frac{d^2}{2e + 32\alpha^2\gamma^2Ld/3} \bigg),
    \end{equation*} for any $d, e > 0$. Choosing $e = E\log\big(\frac{6T}{\delta}\big)$ for some $E > 0$ (to be specified later) and  
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:bound-B2}
        d = \log\bigg(\frac{6T}{\delta}\bigg)\Bigg(\frac{16}{3}\alpha^2\gamma^2L + \sqrt{\frac{256}{9}\alpha^4\gamma^4L^2 + 2E}\Bigg),    
    \end{equation} results in $2\exp\Big(-\frac{d^2}{2e + 32\alpha^2\gamma^2Ld/3} \Big) = \frac{\delta}{3T}$. Further, under $\Gamma_N$, it holds that
    \begin{align*}
        \sum_{t \in [N]}\mathbb{E}_t\big[(2\alpha^2L\theta^t)^2\big] &\stackrel{(i)}{\leq} 16\alpha^2\gamma^2L\sum_{t \in [N]}\mathbb{E}_t|2\alpha^2L\theta^t| \stackrel{(ii)}{\leq} 32\alpha^4\gamma^2L^2\sum_{t \in [N]}\mathbb{E}_t\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 \\
        &\leq \frac{576\alpha^4\gamma^{4-p}\sigma^pL^2N}{n} \leq \frac{576\alpha^4\gamma^{4-p}\sigma^pL^2T}{n},
    \end{align*} where $(i)$ follows from $|2\alpha^2L\theta^t| \leq 16\alpha^2\gamma^2L$, in $(ii)$ we used $\mathbb{E}|X-\mathbb{E} X| \leq 2\mathbb{E} X$ for a non-negative random variable, while $(iii)$ follows from Lemma \ref{lm:noise-behavior}. Therefore, choosing $E = \frac{576\alpha^4\gamma^{4-p}\sigma^pL^2T}{n}$, defining the event $\Xi_2 = \big\{\omega: B_2(\omega) \leq d \big\}$ where $d$ is given in \eqref{eq:bound-B2} and following similar steps as in the previous case, it can be shown that $\mathbb{P}(\Gamma_N \cap \Xi_1 \cap \Xi_2) \geq 1 - \frac{(N-1/3)\delta}{T}$.
    
    \paragraph{Bounding $B_3$.} Finally, consider the term $B_3 = \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{t \in [N]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\eta^t_i$, where $\eta^t_i = \|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,u}\|^2 - \mathbb{E}_t\|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,u}\|^2$. By definition, we know that $\mathbb{E}_t[\eta^t_i] = 0$ and $\Big|\frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\eta^t_i\Big| \leq \frac{96\alpha^3\gamma^2\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}$, hence we can apply Lemma \ref{lm:freedman}, to get
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathbb{P}\bigg(\big|B_3 \big| > g \text{ and } \sum_{t \in [N]}\mathbb{E}_t\bigg(\frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{i \in [n]}\eta^t_i\bigg)^2 \leq h \bigg) \leq 2\exp\bigg(-\frac{g^2}{2h + 192\alpha^3\gamma^2\lambda^2L^2g/3n(1-\lambda^2)^2} \bigg),
    \end{equation*} for any $g,h > 0$. Moreover, from Assumption \ref{asmpt:noise} we can conclude that $\{\eta^t_i\}_{i \in [n]}$ are independent conditioned on $\mathcal{F}_t$. Combined with $\mathbb{E}_t[\eta^t_i] = 0$, it follows that on $\Gamma_N$
    \begin{align*}
        &\sum_{t \in [N]}\mathbb{E}_t\bigg(\frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{i \in [n]}\eta^t_i\bigg)^2 = \frac{144\alpha^6\lambda^4L^4}{n^2(1-\lambda^2)^4}\sum_{t \in [N]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\mathbb{E}_t\big[(\eta^t_i)^2\big] \\
        &\stackrel{(i)}{\leq} \frac{1152\alpha^6\gamma^2\lambda^4L^4}{n^2(1-\lambda^2)^4}\sum_{t \in [N]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\mathbb{E}_t\big[|\eta^t_i|\big] \stackrel{(ii)}{\leq} \frac{2304\alpha^6\gamma^2\lambda^4L^4}{n^2(1-\lambda^2)^4}\sum_{t \in [N]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\mathbb{E}_t\|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,u}\|^2 \\
        &\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad \stackrel{(iii)}{\leq} \frac{41472\alpha^6\gamma^{4-p}\sigma^p\lambda^4L^4N}{n(1-\lambda^2)^4} \leq \frac{41472\alpha^6\gamma^{4-p}\sigma^p\lambda^4L^4T}{n(1-\lambda^2)^4},
    \end{align*} where in $(i)$ we used the fact that $|\eta^t_i| \leq 8\gamma^2$, $(ii)$ follows from $\mathbb{E}|X - \mathbb{E} X| \leq 2\mathbb{E} X$ for $X \geq 0$, while in $(iii)$ we used Lemma \ref{lm:sadiev}. Following the same reasoning as in the previous two cases, it can be seen that choosing $h = H\log\big(\frac{6T}{\delta}\big)$, where $H = \frac{41472\alpha^6\gamma^{4-p}\sigma^p\lambda^4L^4T}{n(1-\lambda^2)^4}$ and  
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:bound-B3}
        g = \log\bigg(\frac{6T}{\delta}\bigg)\Bigg(\frac{32\alpha^3\gamma^2\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2} + \sqrt{\frac{1024\alpha^6\gamma^4\lambda^4L^4}{n^2(1-\lambda^2)^4} + 2H}\Bigg), 
    \end{equation} results in $2\exp\Big(-\frac{g^2}{2h + 192\alpha^3\gamma^2\lambda^2L^2g/3n(1-\lambda^2)^2} \Big) = \frac{\delta}{3T}$. Therefore, defining $\Xi_3 = \{\omega: B_3(\omega) \leq g\}$ and following similar reasoning as before, it can be concluded that
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:desired-probability-bound}
        \mathbb{P}(\Gamma_N \cap \Xi_1 \cap \Xi_2 \cap \Xi_3) \geq 1 - \frac{N\delta}{T}.
    \end{equation}
    
    \paragraph{Completing the induction.} Consider the event $\Gamma_N \cap \Xi_1 \cap \Xi_2 \cap \Xi_3$. From \eqref{eq:desired-probability-bound} we know that $\mathbb{P}(\Gamma_N \cap \Xi_1 \cap \Xi_2 \cap \Xi_3) \geq 1 - \frac{N\delta}{T}$, while from \eqref{eq:induction-step-2} we know that on this event 
    \begin{align}\label{eq:induction-step-3}
        &\Delta_{N+1} \leq \Delta_1 + b + d + g + \frac{36\alpha^2\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^pLT}{n} + \frac{8\alpha\sigma^{2p}T}{\gamma^{2(p-1)}} \nonumber \\
        &+ \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2A^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2} + \frac{48\alpha^3\sigma^{2p}\lambda^2L^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2\gamma^{2(p-1)}} + \frac{216\alpha^3\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^p\lambda^2L^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2},
    \end{align} where $b,d,g$ are given in \eqref{eq:bound-B1}, \eqref{eq:bound-B2} and \eqref{eq:bound-B3}. Note that if we can choose $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ such that the right-hand side in \eqref{eq:induction-step-3} is less than or equal to $2\Delta_1$, it would then follow that on $\Gamma_N \cap \Xi_1 \cap \Xi_2 \cap \Xi_3$ we have $\Delta_{N+1} \leq 2\Delta_1$, hence $\Gamma_N \cap \Xi_1 \cap \Xi_2 \cap \Xi_3 \subseteq \Gamma_{N+1}$ and $\mathbb{P}(\Gamma_{N+1}) \geq \mathbb{P}(\Gamma_N \cap \Xi_1 \cap \Xi_2 \cap \Xi_3) \geq 1 - \frac{N\delta}{T}$, completing the induction. Therefore, our aim is to show that there exist $\alpha,\gamma$ such that
    \begin{align}\label{eq:induction-step-4}
        b &+ d + g + \frac{36\alpha^2\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^pLT}{n} + \frac{8\alpha\sigma^{2p}T}{\gamma^{2(p-1)}} + \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2A^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2} \nonumber \\
        &+ \frac{48\alpha^3\sigma^{2p}\lambda^2L^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2\gamma^{2(p-1)}} + \frac{216\alpha^3\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^p\lambda^2L^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2} \leq \Delta_1,
    \end{align} where $b,d,g$ are given in \eqref{eq:bound-B1}, \eqref{eq:bound-B2} and \eqref{eq:bound-B3}. Let the clipping threshold and step-size satisfy $\gamma \geq \max\Big\{2A + 4B\sqrt{L\Delta_1} + \frac{2\lambda L\sqrt{n}}{1-\lambda}, (nT)^{\frac{1}{3p-2}} \Big\}$ and 
    \begin{equation*}
        \alpha \leq \min\bigg\{C_1n^{\frac{2p-1}{3p-2}}T^{\frac{1-p}{3p-2}}\gamma^{-1}, C_2n^{\frac{p}{3(3p-2)}}T^{\frac{2(1-p)}{3(3p-2)}}\gamma^{-\frac{2}{3}}, \frac{1}{2L}, \frac{1-\lambda^2}{8\lambda LB\sqrt{3}} \bigg\},
    \end{equation*} for some $C_1,C_2 > 0$. It can then be verified that $\alpha^2\gamma^{2-p} \leq nC_1^{2}T^{-1}$, $\alpha\gamma^{2(1-p)} \leq C_1T^{-1}$ and $\alpha^3\gamma^{2-p} \leq C_2^3T^{-1}$, hence choosing $C_1 \leq \min\Big\{\frac{\sqrt{\Delta_1}}{12\sigma^{\nicefrac{p}{2}}\sqrt{2L}}, \frac{\Delta_1}{64\sigma^{2p}} \Big\}$, $C_2 \leq \frac{\Delta_1^{1/3}(1-\lambda^2)^{2/3}}{12\sigma^{p/3}\lambda^{2/3}L^{2/3}}$ and $\alpha \leq \min\bigg\{\sqrt[3]{\frac{(1-\lambda^2)^2\Delta_1}{96\lambda^2L^2A^2T}},\frac{1-\lambda^2}{\lambda L\sqrt{6}}\bigg\}$, it can be verified that \eqref{eq:induction-step-4} becomes $b + d + g \leq \frac{3\Delta_1}{8}$. We now bound each of these terms. First, recall that
    \begin{equation*}
        b = \log\bigg(\frac{6T}{\delta}\bigg)\Bigg(\frac{4}{3}\alpha\gamma\sqrt{L\Delta_1} + \sqrt{\frac{16}{9}\alpha^2\gamma^2L\Delta_1 + 2C}\Bigg),    
    \end{equation*} where $C = \frac{72\alpha^2\gamma^{2-p}\sigma^pL\Delta_1T}{n} \leq 72C_1^2\sigma^pL\Delta_1$. Further, if $\alpha \leq C_3\gamma^{-1}$, where $C_3 \leq \frac{3\sqrt{\Delta_1}}{64\log(\frac{6T}{\delta})\sqrt{2L}}$ and $C_1 \leq \frac{\sqrt{\Delta_1}}{192\log(\frac{6T}{\delta})\sigma^{p/2}\sqrt{2L}}$, it follows that
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:bound-1}
        b \leq \log\bigg(\frac{6T}{\delta}\bigg)\Bigg(\frac{4}{3}C_3\sqrt{L\Delta_1} + \sqrt{\frac{16}{9}C_3^2L\Delta_1 + 144C_1^2\sigma^pL\Delta_1}\Bigg) \leq \frac{\Delta_1}{8}.
    \end{equation} Next, recall that 
     \begin{equation*}
        d = \log\bigg(\frac{6T}{\delta}\bigg)\Bigg(\frac{16}{3}\alpha^2\gamma^2L + \sqrt{\frac{256}{9}\alpha^4\gamma^4L^2 + 2E}\Bigg),    
    \end{equation*} where $E = \frac{576\alpha^4\gamma^{4-p}\sigma^pL^2T}{n} \leq 576C_1^2C_3^2\sigma^pL^2 \leq \frac{288C_3^2L\Delta_1}{192^2\log^2(\frac{6T}{\delta})}$. From the previous choice of $C_3$, it can be verified that
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:bound-2}
        d \leq \log\bigg(\frac{6T}{\delta}\bigg)\Bigg(\frac{16}{3}C_3^2L + \sqrt{\frac{256}{9}C_3^4L^2 + \frac{C_3^2L\Delta_1}{64\log^2(\frac{6T}{\delta})}}\Bigg) \leq \frac{\Delta_1}{8}.
    \end{equation} Finally, recall that   
    \begin{equation*}
        g = \log\bigg(\frac{6T}{\delta}\bigg)\Bigg(\frac{32\alpha^3\gamma^2\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2} + \sqrt{\frac{1024\alpha^6\gamma^4\lambda^4L^4}{n^2(1-\lambda^2)^4} + 2H}\Bigg), 
    \end{equation*} where $H = \frac{41472\alpha^6\gamma^{4-p}\sigma^p\lambda^4L^4T}{n(1-\lambda^2)^4} \leq \frac{41472\alpha^2C_1^2C_3^2\sigma^p\lambda^4L^4}{(1-\lambda^2)^4} \leq \frac{9\Delta_1\alpha^2C_3^2\lambda^4L^3}{16(1-\lambda^2)^4\log^2(\frac{6T}{\delta})} \leq \frac{\Delta_1C_3^2L}{64\log^2(\frac{6T}{\delta})}$, where the last inequality follows from $\alpha \leq \frac{(1-\lambda^2)^2}{6\lambda^2L}$. Using the same step-size condition, we then have
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:bound-3}
        g \leq \log\bigg(\frac{6T}{\delta}\bigg)\Bigg(\frac{16C_3^2L}{3} + \sqrt{\frac{256}{9}C_3^4L^2 + \frac{C_3^2L\Delta_1}{32\log^2(\frac{6T}{\delta})}} \Bigg) \leq \frac{\Delta_1}{8}.
    \end{equation} Combining \eqref{eq:bound-1}, \eqref{eq:bound-2} and \eqref{eq:bound-3}, we finally get $b + d + g \leq \frac{3\Delta_1}{8}$, completing the proof.

body_md:
Starting from Lemma \ref{lm:descent-sharp}, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{\alpha}{16n}&\sum_{t \in [T]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\nabla f(x^t_i)\|^2 \leq \Delta_1 - \Delta_{T+1} - \alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\langle \nabla f(\overline{x}^t), \widehat{g}^t_u\rangle + 2\alpha^2L\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 \\
        &+ 2\alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_b\|^2 + \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2A^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2} + \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{i \in [n]}\sum_{t \in [T]}\big(\|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,b}\|^2 + \|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,u}\|^2\big).
    \end{align*} Using Lemma \ref{lm:desirable-event}, we know that, with probability at least $1 - \delta$
    \begin{align*}
        &\frac{\alpha}{16n}\sum_{t \in [T]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\nabla f(x^t_i)\|^2 \leq \Delta_1 - \Delta_{T+1} - \alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\langle \nabla f(\overline{x}^t), \widehat{g}^t_u\rangle + 2\alpha^2L\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_u\|^2 \\
        &+ 2\alpha\sum_{t \in [T]}\|\widehat{g}^t_b\|^2 + \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2A^2T}{(1-\lambda^2)^2} + \frac{12\alpha^3\lambda^2L^2}{n(1-\lambda^2)^2}\sum_{i \in [n]}\sum_{t \in [T]}\big(\|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,b}\|^2 + \|\widetilde{g}^t_{i,u}\|^2\big) \leq 2\Delta_1.
    \end{align*} Dividing both sides by $\frac{\alpha T}{16}$, we get that, with probability at least $1 - \delta$
    \begin{equation*}
        \frac{1}{nT}\sum_{t \in [T]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\nabla f(x^t_i)\|^2 \leq \frac{32\Delta_1}{\alpha T}.
    \end{equation*} We now consider the different conditions on the step-size and clipping threshold. First, if $\alpha = \textit{constant}$, the above bound evaluates to (in the worst-case with respect to $n$ and $1-\lambda$)
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:bound-case-1}
        \frac{1}{nT}\sum_{t \in [T]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\nabla f(x^t_i)\|^2 = \mathcal{O}\bigg( \frac{1}{(1-\lambda^2)^2T}\bigg).
    \end{equation} Next, if $\alpha = \frac{(1-\lambda^2)^{2/3}\Delta_1^{1/3}}{2(\lambda LA)^{2/3}T^{1/3}\sqrt[3]{12}}$, then
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:bound-case-2}
        \frac{1}{nT}\sum_{t \in [T]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\nabla f(x^t_i)\|^2 = \mathcal{O}\bigg( \frac{1}{(1-\lambda^2)^{2/3}T^{2/3}}\bigg).
    \end{equation} Third, if $\alpha = C_1n^{\frac{2p-1}{3p-2}}T^{\frac{1-p}{3p-2}}\gamma^{-1}$, then 
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:bound-case-3}
        \frac{1}{nT}\sum_{t \in [T]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\nabla f(x^t_i)\|^2 = \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\Bigg(\max\Bigg\{\frac{1}{(1-\lambda)n^{\frac{p}{6p-4}}T^{\frac{2p-1}{3p-2}}},\frac{1}{(nT)^{\frac{2(p-1)}{3p-2}}}\Bigg\}\Bigg).
    \end{equation} Fourth, if $\alpha = C_2n^{\frac{p}{3(3p-2)}}T^{\frac{2(1-p)}{3(3p-2)}}\gamma^{-2/3}$, then
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:bound-case-4}
        \frac{1}{nT}\sum_{t \in [T]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\nabla f(x^t_i)\|^2 = \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\Bigg(\max\Bigg\{\frac{n^{\frac{2(p-1)}{3(3p-2)}}}{(1-\lambda)^{\frac{4}{3}}T^{\frac{7p-4}{3(3p-2)}}},\frac{n^{\frac{2-p}{3(3p-2)}}}{(1-\lambda^2)^{\frac{2}{3}}T^{\frac{7p-6}{3(3p-2)}}}\Bigg\}\Bigg).
    \end{equation} Finally, the only remaining case is that of $\alpha = C_3\gamma^{-1}$, where we get 
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:bound-case-5}
        \frac{1}{nT}\sum_{t \in [T]}\sum_{i \in [n]}\|\nabla f(x^t_i)\|^2 = \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\Bigg(\max\Bigg\{\frac{\sqrt{n}}{(1-\lambda)T}, \frac{n^{\frac{1}{3p-2}}}{T^{\frac{3(p-1)}{3p-2}}}\Bigg\}\Bigg).
    \end{equation} The proof is completed by combining \eqref{eq:bound-case-1}-\eqref{eq:bound-case-5}.
